edits.text: PRELIMINARY STATEMENT. This proposed draft sets out the framework for Defendant’s responses to Plaintiff’s First Requests for Production. Before service, Defendant will complete a separate response to each request, specifying the scope of the search and production, each objection and its particular grounds, and whether responsive materials are being withheld on that basis.

1. REQUEST-SPECIFIC OBJECTIONS. Each objection will be stated with specificity in the response to the applicable request, together with its grounds and a statement whether responsive materials are being withheld on that basis. Any objection limited to part of a request will identify the disputed portion, and Defendant will respond to the remainder. Claims of attorney-client privilege, work-product protection, or other applicable protection will be identified in the applicable response and supported by the information required under applicable rules or court orders.

2. SEARCH AND PRODUCTION. Each request-specific response will describe the scope of Defendant’s reasonable search and proposed production, including applicable custodians, sources, date ranges, and material search limitations, as relevant, and identify any scope limitation resulting from an objection. Defendant will begin rolling production of responsive, non-privileged materials within 14 days after agreement on these production provisions and complete production within 30 days after that agreement. These provisions do not extend any earlier deadline imposed by applicable rules or court orders. Plaintiff retains all rights to challenge objections, search or production limitations, or the adequacy of production, and to seek relief.

3. PRIVILEGE LOG. Defendant will provide any privilege log required by applicable rules or court orders no later than 30 days after agreement on these production provisions, or by any earlier governing deadline. The log will describe withheld materials and the asserted protection with sufficient information to permit assessment of the claim without disclosing protected information.

4. SUPPLEMENTATION. Defendant will supplement its responses and production as required by applicable rules or court orders. This supplementation provision does not defer the production commitments above or excuse an incomplete search or production.
